newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Dec housing starts fall 1.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: Canada Dec housing starts fall 1.1 pct.

text.p: Canadian housing starts fell by 1.1 percent in December to a seasonally adjusted annual rate (SAAR) of 136,500 units from a revised 138,000 units in November, the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corp (CMHC) said on Thursday.
A Reuter survey of economists had forecast housing starts of 135,720 units.
Actual housing starts fell to 10,324 in December from 12,144 the month before. The SAAR is a monthly figure adjusted to remove normal seasonal variation and multiplied by 12.

The housing corporation said despite the decline in housing starts in December, housing activity has been "noticeably higher" in the last months of 1996.

"Construction of single detached homes, in particular, has now reached its fastest pace since September 1994," Michel Laurence, senior economist at the CMHC market analysis center, said in a statement. "This segment is expected to increase further in 1997 as home ownership remains attractive with low new house prices and low mortgage rates."
